scenes.tts: A neuron's layer is one record of its birthday. What else does a birthday leave behind?
scenes.visual: Title card: What a Birthday Leaves Behind. A finished cortical column.
scenes.narration: A neuron's layer is one record of its birthday. What else does a birthday leave behind?

scenes.tts: Each layer's neurons carry identity genes that serve as markers. Markers read identity without knowing position.
scenes.visual: Neurons in the column light up with marker colours, then are lifted out of the column and keep their colours.
scenes.narration: Each layer's neurons carry identity genes that serve as markers. Markers read identity without knowing position.

scenes.tts: In mouse, T B R one is high in subplate and layer six neurons.
scenes.caption: In mouse, Tbr1 is high in subplate and layer 6 neurons.
scenes.visual: Tbr1 colour on subplate and layer 6.
scenes.narration: In mouse, Tbr1 is high in subplate and layer 6 neurons.

scenes.tts: C tip two and Fez F two are high in layer five neurons that project below the cortex.
scenes.caption: Ctip2 and Fezf2 are high in layer 5 neurons that project below the cortex.
scenes.visual: Ctip2/Fezf2 colour on layer 5 neurons with axons heading down out of the cortex.
scenes.narration: Ctip2 and Fezf2 are high in layer 5 neurons that project below the cortex.

scenes.tts: Sat B two marks callosal neurons, which send axons to the other hemisphere. Most sit in the upper layers.
scenes.caption: Satb2 marks callosal neurons, which send axons to the other hemisphere. Most sit in the upper layers.
scenes.visual: Satb2 colour on neurons with axons crossing to the other hemisphere, mostly in upper layers.
scenes.narration: Satb2 marks callosal neurons, which send axons to the other hemisphere. Most sit in the upper layers.

scenes.tts: Expression overlaps, and position alone does not define a class.
scenes.visual: Colour zones blend at their edges. Label: markers overlap.
scenes.narration: Expression overlaps, and position alone does not define a class.

scenes.tts: The cortical schedule so far describes excitatory neurons made by dorsal progenitors. They release glutamate.
scenes.visual: Column labelled excitatory, glutamate, dorsal progenitors.
scenes.narration: The cortical schedule so far describes excitatory neurons made by dorsal progenitors. They release glutamate.

scenes.tts: Cortical interneurons release gaba. In rodents, most are born in the ganglionic eminences of the ventral forebrain.
scenes.caption: Cortical interneurons release GABA. In rodents, most are born in the ganglionic eminences of the ventral forebrain.
scenes.visual: Coronal forebrain outline; ganglionic eminences highlighted; interneurons labelled GABA.
scenes.narration: Cortical interneurons release GABA. In rodents, most are born in the ganglionic eminences of the ventral forebrain.

scenes.tts: They travel up into the cortex. For most cortical neurons in rodents, a dorsal birthplace means excitatory, a ventral one inhibitory.
scenes.visual: Interneurons stream tangentially into the cortex. Labels: dorsal = excitatory, ventral = inhibitory (most cortical neurons, rodents).
scenes.narration: They travel up into the cortex. For most cortical neurons in rodents, a dorsal birthplace means excitatory, a ventral one inhibitory.

scenes.tts: Interneurons from the medial ganglionic eminence follow a similar birthdate rule, settling inside out. Not every interneuron does.
scenes.visual: Medial ganglionic eminence interneurons settle inside out by birthdate. A small note: not every interneuron.
scenes.narration: Interneurons from the medial ganglionic eminence follow a similar birthdate rule, settling inside out. Not every interneuron does.

scenes.tts: One question is still open. Does a mammalian progenitor run a clock like the fly's?
scenes.visual: Fly clock icon beside a mouse progenitor with a question mark.
scenes.narration: One question is still open. Does a mammalian progenitor run a clock like the fly's?

scenes.tts: Predict. Grow one early progenitor alone in a dish, with no cortex around it. Does it still make neurons in order?
scenes.visual: A single progenitor in a culture dish. Predict card: deep-layer markers first, or no order?
scenes.narration: Predict. Grow one early progenitor alone in a dish, with no cortex around it. Does it still make neurons in order?

scenes.tts: Sally Temple's laboratory did this in two thousand six. The clones made deep-layer markers before later markers.
scenes.caption: Sally Temple's laboratory did this in 2006. The clones made deep-layer markers before later markers.
scenes.visual: Credit: Shen and colleagues, Temple laboratory, 2006. The clone makes deep-layer-marker neurons first, later-marker neurons after.
scenes.narration: Sally Temple's laboratory did this in 2006. The clones made deep-layer markers before later markers.

scenes.tts: That points to a schedule within the lineage.
scenes.visual: Calendar icon inside the lone progenitor.
scenes.narration: That points to a schedule within the lineage.

scenes.tts: Relatives of the fly factors do have timing jobs in mouse. But a full cascade like the fly's has not been shown in cortex.
scenes.visual: Fly factor icons beside mouse relatives with timing jobs. Label: full cascade not shown in cortex.
scenes.narration: Relatives of the fly factors do have timing jobs in mouse. But a full cascade like the fly's has not been shown in cortex.

scenes.tts: It could be a cascade. Or it could be a gradual change in competence, shaped by feedback from neurons already made.
scenes.visual: Two options side by side: a factor cascade; a slowly changing menu with feedback arrows from neurons already made. Label: open.
scenes.narration: It could be a cascade. Or it could be a gradual change in competence, shaped by feedback from neurons already made.

scenes.tts: Now return to the one idea. The progenitor's state at a birthday sets the neuron's temporal identity, its layer included.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card returns.
scenes.narration: Now return to the one idea. The progenitor's state at a birthday sets the neuron's temporal identity, its layer included.

scenes.tts: The pulse dated birthdays. The ferret grafts showed laminar fate is set late, cues included, and that the menu shortens.
scenes.visual: Three puzzle cards return; cards 1 and 2 tick off with the pulse and the graft icons.
scenes.narration: The pulse dated birthdays. The ferret grafts showed laminar fate is set late, cues included, and that the menu shortens.

scenes.tts: The fly showed what a temporal state can be made of. And Q counted how one pool is built and then spent.
scenes.visual: The fly clock icon and the Q curve; card 3 ticks off.
scenes.narration: The fly showed what a temporal state can be made of. And Q counted how one pool is built and then spent.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: a birthday is a timestamp. What the progenitor can make then, and the cues it reads, set the neuron's temporal identity.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card over the finished column.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: a birthday is a timestamp. What the progenitor can make then, and the cues it reads, set the neuron's temporal identity.
